The V-C35 registry action still lists nine steps including 'Business-user portal'. The app has eight: Business Users is a section of the Authentication step, and an old /welcome?step=portal link opens Authentication with Business Users expanded (welcome.tsx welcomeLoader). The Setup checklist keeps its 'Business-user portal' row, which opens Settings → Advanced → Authentication. The walkthrough should read the registry action as the eight-step flow; the registry text needs an update by the batch owner.
The SET-004 M33/6 addendum in docs/decision-records/DECISIONS-SETTINGS.md still says nine steps; the SET-004 2026-09-15 amendment is the current shape.

Observation for the owner, not a recorded contradiction: the wizard and setup drafts keep typed secrets (setup password, SMTP password, SSO client secret, DocuSign RSA private key and Connect HMAC secret, AI API key) in sessionStorage for the tab until they are saved, setup finishes, or the Administrator signs out (setup-drafts.ts, welcome.tsx useSetupDraft, setup.tsx). The guide describes this only as 'unfinished entries'.

The V-C37 expected result 'An Administrator with a password keeps emergency password sign-in when Email and password is off' holds only while Legal User Authentication keeps another method. After the last identity provider is removed from an SSO-only Legal policy, the API still accepts the Administrator's password but the staff sign-in page offers no form (see productBugs).

The fresh-install display mismatch in productBugs was found by reading the code, not by running it. The walkthrough can confirm it on the unseeded lab: finish the wizard without adding a domain, change a staff account to Business user, and try Business Portal sign-in.

productBugs: apps/web/src/routes/login.tsx initialView/'unavailable' view with apps/api/src/modules/auth/routes.ts DELETE /auth/sso-providers (3e91951f): removing the last identity provider turns off legal.sso even when it is the only Legal method (sso.test.ts asserts this). The staff sign-in page then shows 'Sign-in is unavailable. Contact your administrator.' with no Administrator sign-in link, so an Administrator without a live session cannot reach the password form. Contradicts TECH-008 break-glass ('a broken or misconfigured IdP must not lock the org out', instance.ts assertPasswordSignIn) and the pane's own 'Administrators retain emergency password sign-in.'

apps/api/src/modules/auth/routes.ts PUT /auth/allowed-domains (3e91951f): emptying the list now turns off every Business sign-in method, which locks out existing Business Users. No decision record covers this. The TECH-008 2026-09-27 addendum and SET-004 say the allowed domains govern new Business User accounts, and DOC-030 documented that existing Business Users keep signing in. The behavior needs an owner decision and a record (the guide now describes the built behavior).

apps/web/src/routes/settings-authentication.tsx (Business card value) and apps/web/src/routes/welcome.tsx (applyAuthentication): with an empty list the panes display Business methods as off, but they never save that state unless the list is emptied through PUT. On a fresh install, authentication_policy is null and the legacy fallback in apps/api/src/auth/authentication-policy.ts keeps business password and magic link on. The wizard sends no Business PATCH when the draft is unchanged. A Business User (for example a staff account changed to Business user) can then sign in on the Business Portal while Settings shows every method off. Contradicts SET-004 (2026-09-15 amendment): the panes expose each group's policy. Found by source inspection, not run.
